title: Control plane connection multiplexer deadlock during mass node drain in Private deployment
creator: Ava Morgan
description: During a routine private cluster node drain that was part of a staged control-plane upgrade, the control plane API servers experienced a hard stall: API requests stopped responding and leader operations stopped progressing for ~18 minutes. This ticket captures the post-incident investigation, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and planned action items to prevent recurrence. The outage affected a subset of Private customers in eu-west who were undergoing a coordinated maintenance window. Impact: API writes were delayed, rolling upgrades failed to complete, and customer workloads experienced transient 503s and scaling delays.
timeline: 2026-02-18 02:03 UTC: Scheduled drain for nodes in eu-west began (orchestrator initiated).

root_cause: A race between the control plane's custom connection multiplexing layer and the node-drain/sock-eviction path caused a lock-order inversion under high watch-connection churn and concurrent TLS renegotiation. Specifically: (1) the mux attempted to hand off sockets while holding a global mux mutex; (2) the drain path attempted to close and requeue sockets while holding a per-connection list lock; (3) TLS renegotiation callbacks triggered additional goroutines that attempted the same lock sequence, producing a deadlock. The deadlock was amplified by an internal unlimited watch reconnect loop and lack of backpressure during mass rescheduling.
mitigations: Emergency: aborted drains and rolled back the staged upgrade within the maintenance window to restore steady-state.

Short-term patch: added a bounded handoff queue + per-connection read deadline to break long-lived blocking reads and allow progressive draining (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/7421).
Operational: temporarily limit concurrent drains to 3 nodes per zone for Private customers until the patch is rolled out.
Observability: added mux queue depth and goroutine-mutex-wait tracing to the control plane canary dashboards (grafana link below).
